Pinnacle’s historical challenge

160 years. The child’s life must lead.

Children need abilities they can use to communicate, learn, participate and grow in independence. Pinnacle challenges an approach that starts with a technique, then leaves families to discover how separate gains add up to the life they want for their child.

01

A task improves. The life question remains.

A child may perform an exercise more successfully while the family still needs to understand what it enables in learning, communication, choice or participation.

02

The family is left to join the parts.

When recommendations are fragmented, parents must work out how separate assessments, specialists and sessions serve the same child’s life.

03

Progress needs a place in real life.

A review needs to ask where an ability is useful, which support the child needs and what to work on next—not only which tasks were completed.

WHO & UNICEF · 2023

WHO and UNICEF’s 2023 report documents unmet needs, fragmented systems, waiting lists and exclusion. It calls for people-centred services and support for caregivers.

Read the independent context ↗
Historical source and comparison scope

160 Years Without a Unified Metric — Pinnacle’s AbilityScore® monograph ↗

The 160-year framing is Pinnacle’s historical argument. These are care problems and decision models, not a finding that every provider failed. WHO–UNICEF documents care gaps; it does not endorse PinnacleAI® or establish its comparative superiority.

The PinnacleAI® philosophy

Your child’s life decides the work.

Self-sufficiency and mainstream participation give the work its direction. At Pinnacle, the life purpose comes first; abilities, goals, methods, specialists, everyday practice and review follow from it.

  1. 1

    Name what matters in life

    Understand the child and family’s priorities for communication, choice, learning, participation and growing independence.

  2. 2

    Understand the abilities

    Use AbilityScore® and the child’s everyday observations to understand the starting point and the support needed.

  3. 3

    Give each goal a purpose

    Make the intended ability observable, so the family can understand what the goal would mean in the child’s life.

  4. 4

    Choose the people and practice

    Select the methods, specialist contributions and everyday programme around those goals, with human guidance.

  5. 5

    Bring learning into daily life

    Parents, caregivers, educators and therapists contribute through the child-specific programme and feedback.

  6. 6

    Review. Learn. Adapt.

    The Personal Development Kernel brings the child’s information and feedback into review. Ask what is becoming useful and let that guide the next decision.

The measure of the work is what it helps make possible in the child’s life.

Self-sufficiency and participation are the purpose of support. Each child’s progress, support needs and outcomes are individual.

Current figures and dated report findings

Pinnacle's owner confirmed this as a current calculated total on 19 September 2026. The component counts supplied do not reproduce 400 billion. A point definition, reproducible calculation, deduplication rules and measurement cutoff have not been supplied. This aggregate is not established by the linked UDIN reports.

Built for 900 million children, parents and families is the mission described in the 7 September 2026 handout, pages 1, 7 and 20. It is not a count of people served or an independently established estimate of unmet need.

2.7B+ · Clinical AI data points
2.7B+ structured developmental events at 17 July 2026 in SRS 4400 annexure p3, item 5. SAE 3000 separately covers a 2.5B+ floor. Clinical AI data points is Pinnacle’s description; the report counts structured events, not necessarily independent clinical observations or AI-training examples.
31M+ · Therapy & developmental services
31,052,382 cumulative services at 17 July 2026 in SRS 4400 annexure p3, item 1. The defined total includes assessments, screenings and parent training. SAE 3000 separately provides limited assurance over the 31M+ floor. This is a volume measure, not a successful-outcome count.
10.4M · Calculated report outputs
1.3 million completed assessments × eight reports = 10.4 million report outputs. Pinnacle’s owner confirmed on 19 September 2026 that each assessment produces one cumulative AbilityScore and seven readiness-index reports. This is arithmetic based on that operational statement; a complete report-generation log has not been inspected, and the linked practitioner reports do not establish this report total.
1.3L+ · Intervention techniques
130,000+ techniques, owner-supplied operational update, 19 September 2026. A dated inventory extract has not been inspected. The earlier September handout describes 90,000+. The linked UDIN reports do not verify this updated figure or the separate clinical effectiveness of every technique.

792,614 unique beneficiary/family registrations at 17 July 2026: SRS 4400 annexure p3, item 2. SAE 3000 separately covers the 790,000+ floor. This is the defined registration measure, not an independently verified outcome count.

Pinnacle describes everyday programmes with nine personalised intervention techniques, nine therapeutic goals per service in its programme model, and family/therapist feedback feeding review and correction. These are programme descriptions; no deduplicated totals for programmes, goal assignments or Fusion Module entries were supplied. The 31M+ cumulative service definition also includes assessments, screenings and parent training, so it cannot automatically be multiplied by nine to establish unique therapeutic goals.

These categories describe different, potentially overlapping units. They must not be added or multiplied to imply unique children, independent observations or a verified aggregate. Programme, goal and feedback-entry totals are not quantified here.

Independent practitioner evidence: SAE 3000 limited assurance and SRS 4400 factual findings, with separately defined scopes. Both UDINs were verified Active on 19 September 2026.

You picture a life. We build the plan around it.

Your child expressing a need. Joining a classroom. Taking part in family life. PinnacleAI® connects measurement, people, daily practice and review around the abilities that matter to your child.

Pinnacle Paradigm Shift: one connected plan.
One child. One connected plan.

A shared direction toward self-sufficiency, mainstream participation and a wonderful life.

The parts matter. So does how they work together.

When you picture a car, you picture where it can take you. The engine, steering and wheels each have a job—and need to work together. A child’s support plan needs that connection too: clear goals, coordinated care, practice beyond the session and a way to check what changes.

The evidence behind this approach

What does Pinnacle mean by a paradigm shift?

Pinnacle uses the term for a connected approach to child development: begin with everyday-life goals, measure abilities, agree a personal plan, connect professional support and home practice, then track, correct and reassess. The phrase describes its approach; it is not a claim of worldwide exclusivity.

Read the original record and context

How are parents included in the licensed intended use?

The MD-5 annexure names parents, therapists, educators and caregivers as intended users of non-diagnostic developmental-support software for children aged 0–12. It describes ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting and adaptive therapy-plan support. Family participation works alongside appropriate professional guidance.

Read the original record and context

What connects the approach to self-sufficiency and mainstream life?

The BIS scope names developmental mapping, planning, everyday therapy, tracking and correction, seven readiness indexes, Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion across the full developmental lifecycle. These named functions describe the direction and scope of the system; individual outcomes depend on the child and their care context.

Read the original record and context

What evidence supports the scale behind Pinnacle?

At 17 July 2026, the SRS 4400 report records 2.7 billion+ structured developmental events, 31,052,382 defined cumulative services and 792,614 beneficiary/family registrations. A separate SAE 3000 report provides limited assurance over specified institutional assertions. The claim map links each figure to its source page; these volume measures are distinct from child outcomes.

THE CONNECTED JOURNEY · A ONE-MINUTE GUIDE

See how one observation
can inform the next step.

Section link

Explore the documented process through an illustrative family scenario. This guide uses no child data and does not perform an assessment.

01

Observe

Start with everyday life.

A family wants to help their child express a choice during a familiar routine. They describe what the child already does, what interests them and where support helps.

Family contribution

Everyday observations give the care team context.

Parents and caregivers in the intended use
02

Review

Bring the observations together.

The family and professionals review the starting point and agree a useful goal. Pinnacle describes the Personal Development Kernel as the child-specific record connecting measurements, context and responses.

People + a connected record

The care team checks the goal and the support appropriate to this child.

Personal Development Kernel and human oversight
03

Report

Make the starting point understandable.

The overall AbilityScore® report and seven readiness views help organise the discussion. The important connection is from the report to an agreed everyday goal.

One profile. Seven readiness views.

Explore what each report is for below. No individual child’s results are displayed here.

Read the measurement methods
04

Practise

Turn the goal into guided practice.

The documented Everyday Therapy™ programme links selected techniques with goals. In this illustration, the care team explains a communication activity within a familiar routine and agrees how the family can take part.

Guidance for the people around the child

The activity, support and practice schedule are agreed with the care team.

Everyday Therapy programme description
05

Give feedback

What happened during practice?

Feedback connects the experience at home with the next review. Try either response to see how the discussion can change.

The care team reviews what happened, discusses the activity and support with the family, and agrees what to try next.

For a difficult activity, discuss a smaller step or more support. For an activity the child can manage, discuss a suitable next challenge. These are examples of a review conversation.

An illustrative feedback example

This demonstration does not assess a child, prescribe an activity or generate a treatment plan.

Tracking, correction and human oversight
06

Review again

Use the experience to shape the next plan.

The care team reviews feedback, adjusts goals or support, and discusses the next assessment. Monthly reassessment is described in the reviewed methodology and walkthrough.

Keep the child’s everyday life in view

Look for meaningful changes in communication, routines, learning and participation, alongside the scores.

Reassessment and methodology

Perhaps you want your child to ask for what they need, take part in a family routine or feel more confident with others. The journey begins by understanding their current abilities, then agreeing what to work toward with the care team.

HOW PINNACLEAI® WORKS

Your observations shape the next plan.

PinnacleAI® connects measurement, a child-specific plan, guided everyday practice and feedback. The purpose is practical: help the child build abilities that matter at home, in school and in everyday life.

  1. 01 · Understand

    AbilityScore®

    Bring observations into a structured view of the child’s present abilities and readiness.

  2. 02 · Plan

    Personal Development Kernel + Prognose®

    Connect this child’s history, goals and responses to the next recommendations.

  3. 03 · Practise

    TherapeuticAI® + Everyday Therapy™

    Turn goals into guided activities that the care team and family can put into practice.

  4. 04 · Review & adapt

    Fusion Module + reassessment

    Bring people’s feedback into review, adjust the plan and reassess progress over time.

One child’s history connects each cycle. What the family and professionals observe today informs what they review next.

Explore the part that matters to you

What do the child’s reports explain?

One overall profile. Seven focused readiness reports.

The eight supplied report examples present an overall AbilityScore® and seven readiness indices on a 0–1000 display scale. Together, the overall profile and focused views give the family and care team a shared starting point for discussing priorities and the next plan.

  • AbilityScore® / TherapeuticAI® reportThe overall developmental profile.
  • Speech Readiness IndexA focused view to discuss communication priorities.
  • Behavior Readiness IndexA focused view to discuss behaviour and participation.
  • Motor Readiness IndexA focused view to discuss movement-related abilities.
  • Study/IQ Readiness IndexThe report’s named view of readiness for learning.
  • School Readiness IndexA focused view to discuss preparation and support for school.
  • Self-Sufficiency IndexA focused view to discuss growing everyday independence.
  • Mainstream Readiness IndexA focused view to discuss participation with other people.

Each index report includes an “Assessment By” field. Read the results with the assessment context and care-team explanation. Readiness-index titles are not diagnoses; the Study/IQ Readiness title should not be read as an independently established IQ test.

Report titles checked against eight supplied examples on 19 September 2026. The overall report cover identifies report presentation version V-1.6.9.9. This is a review of report format, not an independent study of outcomes.

This public guide describes the report structure. Children’s identities, individual results and original reports remain private.

Where do parents and the care team fit?

Parents and caregivers contribute observations from everyday life; therapists and educators bring the context they see. The MD-5 intended use explicitly names parents, therapists, educators and caregivers. Their participation connects home routines with professional support.

The reviewed dossier describes the clinical AbilityScore® as clinician-administered and clinically governed. A family questionnaire should therefore be distinguished from the clinical assessment and score.

MD-5 · intended-use annexureEvidence Dossier · page 40
Share thisWhatsApp
XShare image
What is the Personal Development Kernel?

It is the child-specific developmental record described in Pinnacle’s architecture: measurements, goals, responses to activities, environment and history stay connected. That record informs subsequent recommendations, so the next plan can take earlier experience into account.

For a family, the useful question is simple: how did what we observed last time change what we will do next?

Evidence Dossier · pages 48–49Methodology preprint · page 3
Share thisWhatsApp
XShare image
How does a goal become everyday practice?

The documented programme connects selected activities to the child’s goals and abilities. The September handout describes 7–9 daily techniques and a four-day therapy forecast. The methodology preprint describes programmes delivered four days ahead, giving families time to prepare.

The care team should explain the selected activities, demonstration and support appropriate to the child. Programme counts in different publications vary; the agreed individual plan determines what to practise.

September handout · pages 5–7Methodology preprint · page 3
Share thisWhatsApp
XShare image
What happens when an activity is too hard or does not engage the child?

That experience is useful feedback. The methodology preprint describes 1–9-star technique ratings feeding the Personal Development Kernel. The BIS schedule names parent, family, caregiver, therapist and clinical tracking and correction through the Fusion Module. This makes review of the plan part of the described workflow. The dossier describes human oversight of recommendations; technique selection is not left to the system alone.

Illustrative example: the family records difficulty with an agreed communication activity; the care team reviews the observation, adjusts the activity or support, and reviews the response at the next check. This explains the feedback loop; it is not a patient case or a promised result.

Methodology preprint · page 3Company walkthrough · page 35BIS schedule · tracking and correction scopeEvidence Dossier · pages 48, 52–53
Share thisWhatsApp

What should the monthly review make clearer?

Compare the child’s present abilities with earlier assessments, discuss progress and difficulties, and agree the next priorities. The company walkthrough and methodology preprint describe monthly reassessment. A useful review connects the score with observable changes in the child’s daily life.

The BIS scope names seven readiness indexes: School Readiness, Speech Readiness, Motor Readiness, Study IQ Readiness, Behavior Readiness, Self Sufficiency Index and Mainstream Inclusion Index. These names describe the modules; they do not promise school entry or independence.

Company walkthrough · pages 35, 37Methodology preprint · page 3BIS schedule · seven readiness indexes

Who can access the child’s programme?

The company describes parental-consent controls and role-based access for the clinical and caregiving people involved in the child’s programme. Access should support coordinated care while respecting the child and family’s privacy.

The dossier documents the access model. Families can ask their care team which people have access and how permissions and consent are managed for their child.

COMPANY-DESCRIBED LEVELS OF DETAIL

17 domains. 79 abilities. 349 skills.

A broad view of development, organised into abilities and skills that can inform a child-specific plan. The direction is practical: what helps this child communicate, learn, manage daily routines and take part in life?

  1. 17

    Developmental domains

    The broad areas considered in Pinnacle’s framework.

  2. 79

    Abilities

    The capabilities the framework helps organise.

  3. 349

    Skills

    More detailed skills to connect with individual goals.

591 observations · AbilityScore® 0–1000

The company-described observation framework and score support a starting point and subsequent progress review. A child’s plan selects relevant priorities; the totals do not mean every child needs every intervention.

Pinnacle-defined architecture: company walkthrough, page 26; September handout, pages 5–6. The standards below supply classification and terminology; WHO does not define these numerical totals. An item-level domain–ability–skill crosswalk has not been independently audited in this review.

Different starting points. Meaningful everyday goals.

Families may arrive with questions about autism, ADHD, communication, sensory processing, movement, learning or other developmental concerns. Pinnacle’s stated purpose centres on the capabilities that help each child grow toward self-sufficiency and participate in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations they need.

  • Communication and choice

    Express a need, make a choice and connect with other people.

  • Daily-life independence

    Build participation in familiar routines and practise useful daily-living skills.

  • Learning and belonging

    Take part in school, relationships and community with appropriate support.

These are examples of individual goals, not promised results. Professional assessment identifies the support appropriate to each child; diagnosis and medical care remain important where indicated. The licensed software’s scope is non-diagnostic developmental support for ages 0–12, not treatment of every condition.

Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion · BIS scopeAge range and non-diagnostic intended use

Your child’s plan should travel with them.

What happens in a therapy session needs to connect with life at home and school. Assessment, therapy, everyday practice and review are most useful to a family when the people involved understand the same goals.

Pinnacle describes a shared pathway that brings those steps together around your child. Diagnostic information still matters for clinical care and access to support. Alongside it, the plan keeps communication, daily routines, learning, relationships and participation in view.

  6. Monthly AbilityScore refresh + progress review

    06 Reassess and explain the trajectory

    Compare the child’s present abilities with their own earlier assessments and review the next priorities. The company walkthrough describes a monthly AbilityScore refresh; the Whitebook also describes monthly review. The care team should explain the schedule and any child-specific changes.

    For the family: An understandable record of change over time, connected to daily-life goals—not a judgement of the child’s worth.

    07 Grow toward self-sufficiency and participation

    Work toward communication, daily living, learning, relationships and participation in school and community. The BIS scope names seven readiness indexes, including Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion. Continue reassessment and support as needs change.

    For the family: A wonderful life defined with the child and family, including the supports that make participation possible.

Review → adapt → practise → reassess. Progress review feeds the next plan. The direction is growing capability and participation, with continuing human support.

This is Pinnacle’s documented developmental-support approach. PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 is a non-diagnostic Class B SaMD for ages 0–12 under the supplied MD-5. A programme, score or licence does not guarantee independence, school entry or a particular outcome. Inclusion is a right; it is not conditional on a score.

Measurement versions and review cadence

The company walkthrough labels 17 domains, 79 abilities, 349 skills and 591 observations as different layers. The September 2026 handout also describes 349 skills, 17 domains and 591 observations. The earlier Whitebook uses 344 skills across six domains. The dossier acknowledges architecture changes, but a complete crosswalk between versions was not supplied. Newer counts should not be attached retrospectively to validation of an older version.

A 0–1000 score is a company-described developmental measure. It is not a diagnosis, an IQ score, a credit score or a guarantee of future independence. Review the methods and limitations alongside the number.

PINNACLE AT A GLANCE

Measurement. A connected plan.
Support for everyday life.

Section link

Pinnacle Blooms Network is a brand of Bharath Healthcare Laboratories Private Limited. Pinnacle describes a seven-stage child-development pathway connecting ability measurement, child-specific planning, integrated support, parent-guided practice and progress review toward participation and growing independence.

The documented combination brings together non-diagnostic Class B developmental-support software, a BIS scope schedule naming connected software modules, and a centre network with individually traceable source records. These documents explain the approach and its scope; each child’s plan and outcomes remain individual.

PARENTS IN THE LICENSED INTENDED USE

Parents are explicitly included in the licensed intended use.

“The software is intended to assist parents, therapists, educators, and caregivers by providing developmental ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting, and adaptive therapy-plan support for children aged 0–12 years.”

MD-5 MFG/MD/2026/000248 · intended-use annexure · 21 April 2026

Bring guided developmental practice into everyday life. The licensed intended use names parents and caregivers alongside therapists and educators. Families have an explicit role in using the software’s developmental-support functions, with goals and guidance appropriate to their child.

Pinnacle’s Everyday Therapy programme and Fusion Module describe how that participation connects with daily practice, feedback and professional review. The BIS schedule names parent, family and caregiver tracking and correction as part of the connected developmental journey.

Read the MD-5 intended-use annexureRead the BIS connected-module scope
What this wording establishes

The intended use identifies whom the software assists and what it supports. It does not confer professional therapist credentials, register a home as a therapy centre or replace appropriate clinical care. A worldwide exclusivity claim is not established by these documents.

WORDS IN THE ORIGINAL BIS SCHEDULE

“for the full developmental lifecycle of children.”

The schedule names AbilityScore, Prognose®, the Everyday Therapy Programme through TherapeuticAI®, the Fusion tracking and correction module, and seven readiness indexes—including Self Sufficiency and Mainstream Inclusion.

This is the named quality-system and software-module scope. The MD-5 records the device’s four intended functions: ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting and adaptive therapy-plan support. Both documents retain their named software and premises. The MD-5 intended population is ages 0–12; individual outcomes remain subject to the child’s circumstances and support.

Read the full software and developmental-module scope

“Design, development, verification and validation, release, deployment, maintenance, technical support and post-market surveillance of Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), including Pinnacle AI GPT-OS™, and Developmental Support Software (Non-Diagnostic), including developmental ability mapping (Ability Score), prognostic engine Prognose®, Clinical Intervention Every Day Therapy Programme through Therapeutic AI®, Parent, Family, Caregiver, Therapist, Clinical Tracking and Correction Fusion Module, School Readiness, Speech Readiness, Motor Readiness, Study IQ Readiness, Behavior Readiness, Self Sufficiency Index, Mainstream Inclusion Index, 7 readiness indexing and associated digital developmental support modules for the full developmental lifecycle of children.”

THE MEANING BEHIND THE SCALE

2.7 billion+

Structured developmental records.
One child’s journey at a time.

Section link

Company-reported in the 7 September 2026 handout.
Counting basis: database rows/events · cutoff 17 July 2026.

See the dated metric and counting basis

A developmental journey you can follow.

Session entries, assessment observations, technique ratings and other platform events can preserve a record over time. The practical question is how that history helps the care team review your child’s plan.

Volume describes the size of the record system. Useful decisions also depend on data quality, consistent measurement, appropriate use and professional judgement.

This is not a count of unique children, independent clinical-trial observations or verified AI-training examples. A large count alone does not prove clinical effectiveness.
Why do some Pinnacle sources say 2.5 billion+ and others 2.7 billion+?

The July dossier used a 2.5 billion+ floor and retired earlier 2.7 billion wording. The September handout subsequently reports 2.7 billion+ observed row counts. The source review distinguishes the 2.5 billion floor assertion in limited assurance from the 2.7 billion factual row-count finding under agreed procedures. Those procedures do not provide an assurance opinion.

These are dated measures with different reporting roles. Neither should be described as an audited count of AI-training examples. Restricted practitioner reports are not republished here.

TOPIC 11International standardsUnderstand ICD-11, ICF, ICHI and SNOMED CT in context.

INTERNATIONAL LANGUAGE. PERSONAL GOALS.

Structured for understanding.
Designed for connected care.

Section link

Four distinct standards help explain the architecture: health information, functioning and participation, interventions, and clinical terminology. Their value depends on how accurately they are implemented.

World Health Organization

ICD-11 · health information

A common classification and clinical terminology for recording, comparing and aggregating health information. It gives health-related records a consistent reference language.

Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICD-11 reference alignment; this does not make the software diagnostic.

WHO · International Classification of DiseasesPinnacle mapping claims · dossier pages 45–46, 84
Share thisWhatsApp
XShare image

World Health Organization

ICF · functioning and participation

A framework covering body functions and structures, activities, participation and environmental context. It helps keep daily life and the support needed to participate in view.

Pinnacle’s handout and dossier describe ICF mappings. The dossier’s b-code examples describe body functions; activity, participation and environment need their own relevant codes.

WHO · International Classification of Functioning, Disability and HealthPinnacle mapping claims · dossier pages 45–46, 84
Share thisWhatsApp
XShare image

World Health Organization

ICHI · health interventions

A classification for recording and analysing health interventions through their target, action and means. It can help describe what intervention is delivered in a consistent way.

Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICHI intervention coding within its architecture.

WHO · International Classification of Health InterventionsPinnacle mapping claims · dossier pages 45–46, 84
Share thisWhatsApp
XShare image

SNOMED International

SNOMED CT · clinical terminology

A detailed clinical terminology that represents information through concepts, descriptions and relationships. It supports consistent meaning in electronic clinical records.

Pinnacle’s dossier describes SNOMED CT terminology alignment. SNOMED International is the responsible organisation.

SNOMED International · What is SNOMED CT?Pinnacle mapping claims · dossier pages 45–46, 84
Share thisWhatsApp
XShare image

Pinnacle’s framework, connected to international languages

The Evidence Dossier describes mappings to ICD-11, ICF and ICHI, alongside SNOMED CT and LOINC terminology and HL7 FHIR representations. These are company-described architecture and mapping claims. Correctly implemented mappings can support more consistent records, exchange and analysis across settings.

The reviewed evidence does not include a complete item-by-item mapping audit or implementation-conformance report. Classification alignment does not establish WHO, UN or SNOMED endorsement, validate the developmental score, or expand the MD-5 intended use.

Evidence Dossier, pages 45–46, 84 and 86; September handout, pages 6 and 8WHO classification licence · use and endorsement
Share thisWhatsApp
XShare image

DESIGNED FOR WIDER REACH

A population-scale ambition. One child’s life at the centre.

Pinnacle describes a connected developmental-support architecture designed for wider deployment: a common framework, a persistent child-specific record, guided daily practice and human review. Its potential value at scale is continuity—helping families and professionals work from the same developmental direction across home, therapy and school.

What makes “sovereign-ready” and “world-ready” meaningful?

For a health system, sovereign readiness means demonstrable control over data and operations under its own governance requirements. International readiness also needs validated mappings, appropriate local language and workflows, applicable regulatory permissions, and evidence of safe, useful performance in that setting.

  • Local control and accountability

    Document hosting location, data-controller responsibilities, lawful use, consent, access controls and audit trails.

  • Interoperability in practice

    Validate the mappings and test information exchange with the systems that will actually use it.

  • Capacity and real-world value

    Test deployment performance, accessibility and child-centred outcomes in the intended population and setting.

The reviewed MD-5 and BIS scope establish specific regulatory and quality-system foundations. Reported network activity and information-security records add context. Together they support examining the deployment proposition; they are not a sovereign-grade certification or authorisation to operate in every country.

How to interpret reported data volume

The reported 2.7 billion+ structured records count database rows and events. They do not establish a nationally representative population, verified AI-training volume or population-level clinical effectiveness.

What independent external verification supports Pinnacle’s institutional claims?

NPSY & Co., Chartered Accountants, issued an SAE 3000 limited-assurance report and a separate SRS 4400 report of factual findings on 3 September 2026. Both UDINs were verified Active on 19 September 2026: 26200027GMBLXU4868 and 26200027HCNFEI9138. The original ICAI verification receipt and a claim-to-page map are linked here. What is PinnacleAI® GPT-OS licensed for?

The supplied MD-5 lists PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 as a Class B, non-diagnostic developmental-support device. Its scope is tied to the named device, version, intended use and premises; it does not establish diagnostic authority or guarantee clinical outcomes.

Are an MD-3 application and an MD-5 licence the same?

No. MD-3 is an application for a manufacturing licence. MD-5 is the issued manufacturing licence. The original application is reviewed; Class B is recorded on the issued MD-5. The separate issued classification decision copy was not available for inspection.

What is the purpose of the Pinnacle developmental pathway?

Pinnacle’s purpose is to help children grow toward self-sufficiency and participation in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations each child needs. Its tagline is “Every child deserves a wonderful life.” The described approach connects ability measurement, child-specific planning, coordinated intervention, everyday practice, tracking, correction and reassessment. Individual outcomes vary.

What do 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills mean?

Pinnacle describes these as different layers of its developmental framework: 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills, with 591 observations and AbilityScore on a 0–1000 scale. The totals belong to Pinnacle’s architecture, not a WHO-defined numerical hierarchy. Individual plans select relevant priorities. The earlier Whitebook used 344 skills across six domains; validation of an earlier version should not be automatically transferred to the newer framework.

How do daily practice and monthly review connect?

The company sources describe 7–9 daily techniques selected for the child’s programme, human feedback through the Fusion tracking and correction module, and monthly AbilityScore refresh. The care team should explain the child-specific goals, practice guidance, review schedule and any adjustments. This is a programme description, not a guaranteed outcome.

How do ICD-11, ICF, ICHI and SNOMED CT relate to PinnacleAI®?

Pinnacle’s dossier describes architecture and mappings using WHO’s ICD-11, ICF and ICHI, alongside SNOMED CT terminology from SNOMED International. Their roles are health information, functioning and participation, interventions, and consistent clinical meaning. Correct implementation can support interoperability; an item-by-item mapping audit was not supplied. Alignment is separate from endorsement, clinical validation and the licensed device’s intended use.

Read the evidence record

Does Pinnacle focus on a diagnosis or on everyday-life goals?

Families may arrive with questions about autism, ADHD, communication, sensory processing, movement, learning or other developmental concerns. Pinnacle’s stated purpose centres on the capabilities that help each child grow toward self-sufficiency and participate in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations they need. These are examples of individual goals, not promised results. Professional assessment identifies the support appropriate to each child; diagnosis and medical care remain important where indicated. The licensed software’s scope is non-diagnostic developmental support for ages 0–12, not treatment of every condition.

Read the evidence record

Is PinnacleAI® certified as sovereign-grade or authorised worldwide?

The reviewed documents do not establish a sovereign-grade certification or worldwide market authorisation. Pinnacle describes an architecture intended for population-scale developmental support. A specific deployment needs documented local control and governance, validated interoperability, applicable permissions, operational capacity and evidence of performance for that population. MD-5 and BIS provide the particular scopes shown in their records.

Read the evidence record

Are parents and caregivers named in the MD-5 intended use?

Yes. The MD-5 annexure states that PinnacleAI® GPT-OS is intended to assist parents, therapists, educators and caregivers through developmental ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting and adaptive therapy-plan support for ages 0–12. This explicitly includes family users of the licensed software. It does not confer professional therapist credentials or register homes as therapy centres; worldwide exclusivity has not been established.

THE WORDS BEHIND THE DOCUMENTS

Clear terms.
Better questions.

Section link

A practical reading guide to the credentials, report types and international classifications used on this page. Each definition links to its Pinnacle source record.

SaMDSoftware as a Medical Device

Software intended for a medical purpose without being part of a hardware medical device. PinnacleAI® GPT-OS is listed as Class B, non-diagnostic developmental-support software in the supplied MD-5.

Read the source record
MD-3Application for a manufacturing licence

The application submitted for a licence to manufacture Class A or Class B medical devices. An application is a step in the regulatory record; it is not the issued licence.

Read the source record
MD-5Issued manufacturing licence

The issued licence records the named manufacturer, premises, device and intended use. Pinnacle’s supplied MD-5 names PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 for non-diagnostic developmental support, ages 0–12.

Read the source record
BIS scopeBureau of Indian Standards licence and scope schedule

The reviewed BIS record describes the management system and activities within its named scope, including developmental-support software modules. It does not establish every centre’s registration or guarantee clinical outcomes.

Read the source record
HFRHealth Facility Registry

The Health Facility Registry assigns facility identifiers. On 19 September 2026, 56 complete IDs were matched in the authenticated NHPR dashboard; 33 displayed Approved. Other workflow statuses and one masked Draft are shown separately. A directory match is not a finding about current operations, clinical quality or outcomes.

Read the source record
UDINUnique Document Identification Number

An identifier for a practitioner’s document. Both supplied UDINs were matched in the live ICAI portal on 19 September 2026 and showed Active. A UDIN authenticates registered particulars; it does not extend the report’s scope.

Read the source record
SAE 3000Limited-assurance report in this evidence collection

The supplied practitioner report gives limited assurance over specified institutional assertions and counting criteria. Read its dated thresholds and scope; it does not validate every headline statistic or a child’s clinical outcome.

Read the source record
SRS 4400Agreed-upon procedures and factual findings

The supplied report records procedures and findings for defined institutional counts. It does not provide an assurance opinion. Its observed counts and the SAE 3000 assertion floors have different reporting roles.

Read the source record
ICD-11International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision

World Health Organization. A common classification and clinical terminology for recording, comparing and aggregating health information. It gives health-related records a consistent reference language. Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICD-11 reference alignment; this does not make the software diagnostic.

Read the source record
ICFInternational Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health

World Health Organization. A framework covering body functions and structures, activities, participation and environmental context. It helps keep daily life and the support needed to participate in view. Pinnacle’s handout and dossier describe ICF mappings. The dossier’s b-code examples describe body functions; activity, participation and environment need their own relevant codes.

Read the source record
ICHIInternational Classification of Health Interventions

World Health Organization. A classification for recording and analysing health interventions through their target, action and means. It can help describe what intervention is delivered in a consistent way. Pinnacle’s dossier describes ICHI intervention coding within its architecture.

Read the source record
SNOMED CTSNOMED CT clinical terminology

SNOMED International. A detailed clinical terminology that represents information through concepts, descriptions and relationships. It supports consistent meaning in electronic clinical records. Pinnacle’s dossier describes SNOMED CT terminology alignment. SNOMED International is the responsible organisation.

Read the source record
